newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bank shares rise on fund interest.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bank shares rise on fund interest.

text.p: Shares of the six major Canadian banks rose on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday, driven by buying interest from fund investors, analysts said.
They said institutional investors viewed the recent drop in bank share prices as a buying opportunity.

"You possibly have some funds that have a lot of cash after RRSP (tax-protected retirement savings plans) season and were looking for a correction in bank stocks to jump in," one unidentified analyst said.
The rise was led by 0.80 gains in Toronto for Toronto-Dominion Bank to 36.30 and Bank of Nova Scotia to 51.65.
Traders said Canadian bank shares had slumped since the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates on March 25.
After the hike, the Toronto Stock Exchange bank index fell 37.57 points to close at 430.88 points on Friday. By early afternoon on Monday the bank index was up to 437.32.
Bank of Montreal was up 0.60 cents to 49.35, Royal Bank of Canada ahead 0.45 to 54.45, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce up 0.60 to 31.80 and National Bank of Canada up 0.25 to 14.20.
